Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned European leaders Thursday to be wary of discussions between the United States and Russia about a new security arrangement for the continent. “It’s not just about security guarantees for Ukraine. In fact, it’s more about some kind of new security framework between Europe and Russia,” Zelensky told a summit in Dublin. “We are waiting for more details, and Europe needs to pay close attention.” The Ukrainian leader spoke as US envoys were in Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi that failed to make a breakthrough towards ending Russia’s invasion. US representatives have set off alarm bells in Europe by touting a possible new security architecture for the continent as part of the talks — fueling fears Washington could side with Russia. Before launching the war in 2022, the Kremlin delivered an ultimatum to NATO on Europe’s security arrangements which included demands for the alliance to withdraw forces from eastern Europe and stop accepting new members. That was rejected by NATO. At the Dublin summit, France’s President Emmanuel Macron said Paris had got some 40 European countries to sign up to a declaration reaffirming the “key principles” of their security. A draft text seen by AFP said the continent’s security remained based on existing treaties such as the UN charter and NATO’s founding document. The declaration said that “any issue affecting European security must be decided in consultation with the Europeans”. AFP Kindly share this story:
